source.title: In-space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM) State of Play

count_semantics.rule: NASA's webpage reports 621 capability-area entries for the overall 2026 survey. PDF Figure 3 reports 11 functional-area counts summing to 523. The PDF states that activities/technologies can appear in multiple functional areas and Software and Algorithms is a separate cross-cutting area. Reconcile the headline and PDF structures against individual Table 2 and Appendix 9 rows before using either number as a deduplicated denominator.

capture_vocabulary.rendezvous: Orbital manoeuvres reduce separation between two space objects.
capture_vocabulary.proximity_operations: Relative distance and/or orientation is managed between two space objects.
capture_vocabulary.capture: A physical connection is established between two space objects, often using a robotic manipulator.
capture_vocabulary.docking: A rigid connection is established without using a robotic arm.
capture_vocabulary.mating: A general physical connection is established between objects or interfaces.
capture_vocabulary.claim_boundary: A relative-motion position/velocity window is not capture, docking, or mating without separate physical-connection evidence.

fluid_transfer_evidence_notes.storable_fluids: NASA reports multiple demonstrations and operational use, including ISS support.
fluid_transfer_evidence_notes.cryogenic_fluids: NASA describes active development and demonstrations with fluid-specific maturity; storage and transfer are separate claims.
fluid_transfer_evidence_notes.high_pressure_or_supercritical_fluids: Treat as a separate capability/evidence lane; do not infer qualification from storable-fluid operations.
fluid_transfer_evidence_notes.claim_boundary: Storage, thermal control, coupler manipulation, transfer, measurement, and accepted receiver inventory are separate claims.
